tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

9: definitions and proof route. The two stages share one specification and explicit
10: invalidation rules; completing stage one does not require stage two.

24: [installed operation](nl0/references/operation.md) to identify explicit proof inputs,
25: ask once for missing active-phase model/reasoning/speed settings and, for a
26: NL0, full or translation request, an explicit per-case worker count N, then call
27: `nl0/scripts/yui.py run` (or prepare/execute). Retain settings already supplied by
28: the user; do not call a separate intent-classification model. Do not silently
29: choose a worker count from defaults or `auto`; obtain a positive integer or
30: the user's explicit confirmation of a proposed number. N bounds local R-node
31: reviews and, in a separate phase, local Lean proofs. NL0/Audit A and

36: host heartbeat for a bounded check every ten minutes. Record the actual schedule
37: ID, report that mathematical work is still pending, then end the current
38: foreground turn. Never keep the owner active through sleep/poll loops. Each
39: scheduled check ends its turn as well. `DISPATCHED` is not workflow completion.

41: commands; do not claim that a monitor was registered. Frozen author/proof/reviewer
42: stages perform only their assigned roles and never schedule owner monitoring or
43: redispatch the workflow.

62: profile and record every fault/wait; use [operational recovery](nl0/references/operation.md#remote-service-recovery)

167: location map, old/new evidence, pending findings and measured preparation cost.

169: the accepted baseline. Do not launch formalization workers for an unaccepted
170: source revision or reuse task packets bound to the old graph.

173: only afterwards generate worker packets. Shared Lean interface discovery may
174: use this preparation pass, but must not silently mutate the sealed NL0 later.

176: the workflow. The work is bounded by the chosen proof regions and patch size,
177: not a universal minute count. Longer time alone is not a mathematical gap.
178:

180: 
181: The unchanged parent checker still binds ordinary audit v3 to the complete
182: graph. `scripts/source_preparation.py` adds a separate incremental record;
183: it never copies old PASS fields into a forged fresh whole-graph audit.
184: Audit B and `workflow.py` both revalidate that record and all underlying evidence.

189: records, untouched paragraphs and local fact/assumption lifetimes are protected.

191: external uses. A broader refactor is deferred rather than widening this operation.
192: Multiple proposed edits to one consumer must first be merged into one coherent
193: candidate or left unextracted. Legacy test copies remain development evidence.

209:   the exact coverage partition and inherited acceptance/qualifications. It does
210:   not judge natural-language mathematics or authenticate a dishonest reviewer.

213: the parent's `applications` source records remain E/M-only. Do not invent an N

215: substitution is not successful factoring. Derivation labels and fanout guesses

217: 
218: Each cut review binds the exact supplied packet hash. Retain the binding from
219: the generated template and verify it during acceptance. Reusing an actual old
220: review after a record-only change requires identical canonical mathematics and

222: and original cost, and disclose that no new mathematical review occurred.

227: depends on the new producer; unchanged input statements and context permit

100:   the explicit allowlisted nodes/fields have changed.
101:

104: to rereading every mathematical proof. It does not require a new LLM proof of
105: every node, and it does not establish the semantics of a substitution.
106:

108: edited application boundaries need new mathematical review. An unchanged
109: downstream proof whose input statements and conventions are unchanged need not
110: be reconstructed merely because its ancestors have a new producer. Its final
111: acceptance nevertheless depends on the replacement producer being accepted.

113:

115: 
116: This is an incremental review procedure under Audit A's mathematical
117: obligations, not permission to weaken source verification or invent a fresh
118: packet replay. The version-bound receipt limitation below is part of the rule.

127: dependency accounting, scopes, guards and E/M applications, and the normal
128: fresh packet-only replay requirement. The extracted proof may be copied, but
129: its new closed interface and context must actually be checked.

132: or replaying its entire old proof by default:
133:
